CONTRACT SHIPMENT

OTHER BENEFITS AND ALLOCATION
A complete-item claim is assessed under its event mapping even when the same workshop owns other insured equipment. The highest dollar limit in this document is not a selectable alternative. Where two items share a room, damage to one does not create a claim for the other. There is no stacking of benefit limits, no replacement of a part sublimit by a full-item limit, and no deduction of another benefit's deductible. A beneficiary may not reclassify a component as a whole item to obtain a larger ceiling. All facts needed to identify the single claimed item are in the incident file.

DECISION PRIORITY
Check denials in this order: benefit not purchased; incident within waiting period; usage over the benefit maximum; unsafe storage without a valid waiver; report beyond the notice window. Stop at the first applicable reason. If none applies, calculate the payment using the settlement rule. Claims here have no wear or cosmetic-only damage. Do not invent additional exclusions from external insurance practice. These are the complete fictional rules for this file.

ACCOUNTING AND DOCUMENTS
Eligible loss is the approved dollar amount after salvage and depreciation; do not deduct them again. Taxes are included. Deductibles are not premiums, and no premium is recoverable as part of the loss. All currency amounts use US dollars with no exchange conversion. A repaired part remains in its stated category even if a different supplier provided it. The caster set sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

interest.instructions: What is Zenith's economic interest in Topaz? Round to two decimal places.
interest.label: e

state:
CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.
Zenith owns 75.00% of Coral.
Indigo owns 50.00% of Topaz.
Coral owns 50.00% of Topaz.

state:

A complete-item claim is assessed under its event mapping even when the same workshop owns other insured equipment. The highest dollar limit in this document is not a selectable alternative. There is no stacking of benefit limits, no replacement of a part sublimit by a full-item limit, and no deduction of another benefit's deductible. A beneficiary may not reclassify a component as a whole item to obtain a larger ceiling. All facts needed to identify the single claimed item are in the incident file.

Its limit is $800.00; deductible $25.00; the part sublimit is $400.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the fan module. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 14 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 500 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The fan module sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

controller.label: c

interest.instructions: What is Sienna's economic interest in Garnet? Round to two decimal places.

state:
CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.
Onyx owns 35.00% of Garnet.
Sienna owns 51.00% of Onyx.

Quartz owns 20.00% of Garnet.

controller.label: a

state:
CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.
Onyx owns 80.00% of Sienna.
Prairie owns 40.00% of Jasper.
Quartz owns 15.00% of Jasper.
Onyx owns 50.00% of Prairie.

+++ b/tests/test_engines.py

+#!/usr/bin/env python
 
+from __future__ import print_function
+
+import unittest
+
+try:
+    from unittest import mock
+except ImportError:
+    import mock
+
+import imp
+import os.path
+
+
+import engines
+
+
+class TestInit(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_init(self):
+        mock_engines = {}
+
+        mock_listdir = mock.Mock(return_value=(
+                'text_engine.txt',
+                '0_engine.py',
+                '.period_engine.py',
+                '@at_engine.py',
+                '__init__.py',
+                '_underscore_engine.py',
+                'normal_engine.py',
+                'compiled_engine.pyc',
+                'optimized_engine.pyo',
+            ))
+
+        valid_engines = {
+                '_underscore_engine':   ('UnderscoreEngine', 'underscore'),
+                'normal_engine':        ('NormalEngine',     'normal'),
+                'compiled_engine':      ('CompiledEngine',   'compiled'),
+                'optimized_engine':     ('OptimizedEngine',  'optimized'),
+            }
+
+        result_dict = {handle: None for __, (__, handle) in valid_engines.items()}
+
+        def mock_import_module(name, package):
+            self.assertEqual(package, 'engines')
+
+            assert name.startswith('.')
+            name = name[1:]
+
+            module = imp.new_module('%s.%s' % (package, name))
+
+            if name == '__init__':
+                module.Engine = engines.Engine
+            else:
+                self.assertIn(name, valid_engines)
+                class_name, engine_handle = valid_engines[name]
+
+                class MockEngine(engines.Engine):
+                    handle = engine_handle
+
+                MockEngine.__name__ = class_name
+                MockEngine.__qualname__ = class_name
+
+                result_dict[engine_handle] = MockEngine
+                setattr(module, class_name, MockEngine)
+
+            return module
+
+        with mock.patch.object(engines, 'engines', mock_engines), \
+             mock.patch('os.listdir', mock_listdir), \
+             mock.patch('importlib.import_module', mock_import_module):
+            engines._init()
+

+        self.assertDictEqual(mock_engines, result_dict)
+
+

+

+
+        self.assertIsNone(engine.handle)
+
+    def test_apply_not_implemented(self):

Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.

Kestrel owns 35.00% of Sienna.

state:
CONTRACT SHIPMENT

GENERAL SETTLEMENT RULE
Subtract the deductible from eligible loss first, flooring at zero. Apply the benefit limit and any applicable part sublimit to the remaining loss. A part sublimit is an additional ceiling, not money added to the benefit limit. Apply exactly one deductible per claim. For a positive payment, select "part ceiling" if the part sublimit binds strictly below the amount entering the cap operation; otherwise select "benefit ceiling" if the benefit limit binds strictly below that amount; otherwise select "loss based". A tie with loss is loss based. These definitions apply to the actual order of operations above.

DECISION PRIORITY
Check denials in this order: benefit not purchased; incident within waiting period; usage over the benefit maximum; unsafe storage without a valid waiver; report beyond the notice window. Stop at the first applicable reason. If none applies, calculate the payment using the settlement rule. Claims here have no wear or cosmetic-only damage. Do not invent additional exclusions from external insurance practice. These are the complete fictional rules for this file.

OTHER BENEFITS AND ALLOCATION
A complete-item claim is assessed under its event mapping even when the same workshop owns other insured equipment. The highest dollar limit in this document is not a selectable alternative. Where two items share a room, damage to one does not create a claim for the other. There is no stacking of benefit limits, no replacement of a part sublimit by a full-item limit, and no deduction of another benefit's deductible. A beneficiary may not reclassify a component as a whole item to obtain a larger ceiling. All facts needed to identify the single claimed item are in the incident file.

UNSAFE-STORAGE EXCLUSION AND EXCEPTION
An unsafe-storage flag excludes an otherwise covered loss. However, a signed pre-incident storage waiver removes this exclusion for that incident. A post-incident signature is not enough. The waiver affects only unsafe storage; it cannot waive waiting periods, usage limits, purchase status or late reporting. A normal-storage flag never needs a waiver. The incident file explicitly records both the storage status and waiver timing.

BENEFIT B4: handling equipment damage
This benefit applies only to the named event handling equipment damage. A claim for a complete handcart and a claim for its caster set both use this benefit. Its limit is $800.00; deductible $50.00; the part sublimit is $500.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the caster set. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 7 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 800 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The caster set sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

SCHEDULE AND DATES
Inception: 2028-07-04. B1: purchased; B2: purchased; B3: purchased; B4: purchased. Report each incident within 21 elapsed calendar days, inclusive. Same-day reporting counts as zero; weekends count. Claims concern one item and one incident. The incident occurs before policy expiry. The contract has no exhausted annual aggregate or prior claim deduction. Purchase status is determined by this schedule, not by the mere presence of a benefit description.

BENEFIT B2: refrigeration breakdown
This benefit applies only to the named event refrigeration breakdown. A claim for a complete cooler and a claim for its temperature probe both use this benefit. Its limit is $1500.00; deductible $50.00; the part sublimit is $500.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the temperature probe. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 7 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 500 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The temperature probe sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

BENEFIT B1: parcel impact
This benefit applies only to the named event parcel impact. A claim for a complete parcel and a claim for its glass insert both use this benefit. Its limit is $800.00; deductible $25.00; the part sublimit is $400.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the glass insert. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 0 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 1000 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The glass insert sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

ACCOUNTING AND DOCUMENTS
Eligible loss is the approved dollar amount after salvage and depreciation; do not deduct them again. Taxes are included. Deductibles are not premiums, and no premium is recoverable as part of the loss. All currency amounts use US dollars with no exchange conversion. A repaired part remains in its stated category even if a different supplier provided it. Inspection dates, reporting dates and incident dates have different purposes: use the incident date for waiting and the report-minus-incident interval for notice. A preliminary email does not replace the reported date in the file. The listed documents are accepted and no further document requirement remains to resolve.

BENEFIT B3: container water damage
This benefit applies only to the named event container water damage. A claim for a complete container and a claim for its paper label stock both use this benefit. Its limit is $1500.00; deductible $50.00; the part sublimit is $400.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the paper label stock. The complete item has no part sublimit. Usage is measured at incident time.
The paper label stock sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

+#!/bin/bash
+set -ex
 
+# Update the latest-release branch with the most recent tagged release
+
+# we want this to only happen from our repo, not forks
+# check this is not a pull request
+# check we're on the master branch
+
+if [ "$TRAVIS_REPO_SLUG" == "alphagov/govuk_elements" ] && [ "$TRAVIS_PULL_REQUEST" == "false" ] && [ "$TRAVIS_BRANCH" == "master" ]; then
+  # get the version from the version file
+  VERSION_TAG="$(cat VERSION.txt)"
+  echo "Using the most recent tag: $VERSION_TAG and creating a latest-release branch"
+  git config --global user.email "travis@travis-ci.org"
+  git config --global user.name "Travis CI"
+  set +x
+  git remote add deploy-latest-release https://"${GH_TOKEN}"@github.com/alphagov/govuk_elements.git > /dev/null 2>&1
+  set -x
+  # check the remote has been added
+  git checkout -b latest-release v"$VERSION_TAG"
+  git push --force deploy-latest-release latest-release
+  echo "Pushed latest-release branch to GitHub"
+else
+  echo "Not updating the latest-release branch as we're on a branch..."
+fi
+

Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.

BENEFIT B2: sample freezer breakdown
This benefit applies only to the named event sample freezer breakdown. A claim for a complete sample freezer and a claim for its control board both use this benefit. Its limit is $2000.00; deductible $100.00; the part sublimit is $300.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the control board. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 7 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 800 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The control board sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

OTHER BENEFITS AND ALLOCATION
A complete-item claim is assessed under its event mapping even when the same workshop owns other insured equipment. The highest dollar limit in this document is not a selectable alternative. Where two items share a room, damage to one does not create a claim for the other. There is no stacking of benefit limits, no replacement of a part sublimit by a full-item limit, and no deduction of another benefit's deductible. A beneficiary may not reclassify a component as a whole item to obtain a larger ceiling. All facts needed to identify the single claimed item are in the incident file.

BENEFIT B4: pump liquid damage
This benefit applies only to the named event pump liquid damage. A claim for a complete pump and a claim for its seal assembly both use this benefit. Its limit is $1500.00; deductible $25.00; the part sublimit is $200.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the seal assembly. The complete item has no part sublimit. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

UNSAFE-STORAGE EXCLUSION AND EXCEPTION
An unsafe-storage flag excludes an otherwise covered loss. However, a signed pre-incident storage waiver removes this exclusion for that incident. A post-incident signature is not enough. The waiver affects only unsafe storage; it cannot waive waiting periods, usage limits, purchase status or late reporting. A normal-storage flag never needs a waiver. The incident file explicitly records both the storage status and waiver timing.

SCHEDULE AND DATES
Inception: 2028-05-14. B1: purchased; B2: purchased; B3: purchased; B4: purchased. Report each incident within 14 elapsed calendar days, inclusive. Same-day reporting counts as zero; weekends count. Claims concern one item and one incident. The incident occurs before policy expiry. The contract has no exhausted annual aggregate or prior claim deduction. Purchase status is determined by this schedule, not by the mere presence of a benefit description.

BENEFIT B3: lab bench impact
This benefit applies only to the named event lab bench impact. A claim for a complete lab bench and a claim for its glass top both use this benefit. Its limit is $1500.00; deductible $75.00; the part sublimit is $200.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the glass top. The complete item has no part sublimit. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. ACCOUNTING AND DOCUMENTS
Eligible loss is the approved dollar amount after salvage and depreciation; do not deduct them again. Taxes are included. Deductibles are not premiums, and no premium is recoverable as part of the loss. All currency amounts use US dollars with no exchange conversion. A repaired part remains in its stated category even if a different supplier provided it. Inspection dates, reporting dates and incident dates have different purposes: use the incident date for waiting and the report-minus-incident interval for notice. A preliminary email does not replace the reported date in the file. The listed documents are accepted and no further document requirement remains to resolve.

Its limit is $1500.00; deductible $75.00; the part sublimit is $200.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the sensor module. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 0 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 800 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The sensor module sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

GENERAL SETTLEMENT RULE
Subtract the deductible from eligible loss first, flooring at zero. Apply the benefit limit and any applicable part sublimit to the remaining loss. +

state:
CONTRACT EQUIPMENT

BENEFIT B3: microphone liquid damage
This benefit applies only to the named event microphone liquid damage. A claim for a complete microphone and a claim for its wireless capsule both use this benefit. Its limit is $2500.00; deductible $100.00; the part sublimit is $400.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the wireless capsule. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 7 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 1000 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The wireless capsule sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

ACCOUNTING AND DOCUMENTS
Eligible loss is the approved dollar amount after salvage and depreciation; do not deduct them again. Taxes are included. Deductibles are not premiums, and no premium is recoverable as part of the loss. All currency amounts use US dollars with no exchange conversion. A repaired part remains in its stated category even if a different supplier provided it. Inspection dates, reporting dates and incident dates have different purposes: use the incident date for waiting and the report-minus-incident interval for notice. A preliminary email does not replace the reported date in the file. The listed documents are accepted and no further document requirement remains to resolve.

DECISION PRIORITY
Check denials in this order: benefit not purchased; incident within waiting period; usage over the benefit maximum; unsafe storage without a valid waiver; report beyond the notice window. Stop at the first applicable reason. If none applies, calculate the payment using the settlement rule. Claims here have no wear or cosmetic-only damage. Do not invent additional exclusions from external insurance practice. These are the complete fictional rules for this file.

UNSAFE-STORAGE EXCLUSION AND EXCEPTION
An unsafe-storage flag excludes an otherwise covered loss. However, a signed pre-incident storage waiver removes this exclusion for that incident. A post-incident signature is not enough. The waiver affects only unsafe storage; it cannot waive waiting periods, usage limits, purchase status or late reporting. A normal-storage flag never needs a waiver. The incident file explicitly records both the storage status and waiver timing.

BENEFIT B4: stage panel damage
This benefit applies only to the named event stage panel damage. A claim for a complete stage panel and a claim for its sign plate both use this benefit. Its limit is $1500.00; deductible $25.00; the part sublimit is $400.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the sign plate. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 0 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 500 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The sign plate sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

OTHER BENEFITS AND ALLOCATION
A complete-item claim is assessed under its event mapping even when the same workshop owns other insured equipment. The highest dollar limit in this document is not a selectable alternative. Where two items share a room, damage to one does not create a claim for the other. There is no stacking of benefit limits, no replacement of a part sublimit by a full-item limit, and no deduction of another benefit's deductible. A beneficiary may not reclassify a component as a whole item to obtain a larger ceiling. All facts needed to identify the single claimed item are in the incident file.

This benefit applies only to the named event projector failure. A claim for a complete projector and a claim for its battery module both use this benefit. Its limit is $1000.00; deductible $75.00; the part sublimit is $400.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the battery module. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 7 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 500 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. BENEFIT B1: camera impact

Its limit is $2500.00; deductible $50.00; the part sublimit is $200.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the lens unit. The complete item has no part sublimit. state:
CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.
Coral owns 50.00% of Garnet.
Ember owns 50.00% of Garnet.
Delta owns 50.00% of Ember.

+<?php
 
+namespace Wecamp\FlyingLiqourice\Domain;
+
+use Rhumsaa\Uuid\Uuid;
+use Wecamp\FlyingLiqourice\Domain\Game\Coords;
+use Wecamp\FlyingLiqourice\Domain\Game\Grid;
+
+final class GameTest extends \PHPUnit_Framework_TestCase
+{
+
+    /**
+     * @test
+     */
+    public function it_sinks_a_ship()
+    {
+        $gridData = [
+            'fields' => [
+                [
+                    'coords' => [
+                        'x'=>0,
+                        'y'=>0
+                    ],
+                    'ship' => [
+                        'startPoint' => [
+                            'x'=>0,
+                            'y'=>0
+                        ],
+                        'endPoint' => [
+                            'x'=>0,
+                            'y'=>1
+                        ],
+                        'hits' => 0
+                    ],
+                    'shot' => false
+                ],
+                [
+                    'coords' => [
+                        'x'=>0,
+                        'y'=>1
+                    ],
+                    'ship' => [
+                        'startPoint' => [
+                            'x'=>0,
+                            'y'=>0
+                        ],
+                        'endPoint' => [
+                            'x'=>0,
+                            'y'=>1
+                        ],
+                        'hits' => 0
+                    ],
+                    'shot' => false
+                ]
+            ],
+            'ships' => [
+                [
+                    'startPoint' => [
+                        'x'=>0,
+                        'y'=>0
+                    ],
+                    'endPoint' => [
+                        'x'=>0,
+                        'y'=>1
+                    ],
+                    'hits' => 0
+                ]
+            ]
+        ];
+
+        $data = [
+            'width' => 10,
+            'height' => 10,
+            'fields' => $gridData
+        ];
+        $gameData = ['id' => Uuid::uuid4()->toString(), 'locked' => false, 'grid' => $data];
+        $game = Game::fromArray($gameData);
+        $result = $game->fire(Coords::create(0, 0));
+
+        $this->assertEquals('HIT', (string) $result);
+
+        $result = $game->fire(Coords::create(0, 1));
+
+        $this->assertEquals('SINK', (string) $result);
+    }
+}
+

+++ b/scikits/learn/benchmarks/bench_plot_balltree.py
@@ -1 +1,59 @@
 
+from scikits.learn.BallTree import BallTree, knn_brute
+import numpy as np
+from time import time
+
+from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
+import sys
+import pylab as pl
+
+def compare_nbrs(nbrs1,nbrs2):
+    assert nbrs1.shape == nbrs2.shape
+    if(nbrs1.ndim == 2):
+        N,k = nbrs1.shape
+        for i in range(N):
+            for j in range(k):
+                if nbrs1[i,j]==i:
+                    continue
+                elif nbrs1[i,j] not in nbrs2[i]:
+                    return False
+        return True
+    elif(nbrs1.ndim == 1):
+        N = len(nbrs1)
+        return numpy.all(nbrs1 == nbrs2)
+
+N = 1000
+ls = 1 # leaf size
+k = 20
+BT_results = []
+KDT_results = []
+
+for i in range(1, 10):
+    print 'Iteration %s' %i
+    D = i*100
+    M = np.random.random([N, D])
+
+    t0 = time()
+    BT = BallTree(M, ls)
+    d, nbrs1 = BT.query(M, k)
+    delta = time() - t0
+    BT_results.append(delta)
+
+    t0 = time()
+    KDT = cKDTree(M, ls)
+    d, nbrs2 = KDT.query(M, k)
+    delta = time() - t0
+    KDT_results.append(delta)
+
+    # this checks we get the correct result
+    assert compare_nbrs(nbrs1,nbrs2)
+
+xx = 100*np.arange(1, 10)
+pl.plot(xx, BT_results, label='scikits.learn (BallTree)')
+pl.plot(xx, KDT_results, label='scipy (cKDTree)')
+pl.xlabel('number of dimensions')
+pl.ylabel('time (seconds)')
+pl.legend()
+pl.show()
+    
+

+++ b/scripts/resolve_dropbox_conflicts.rb
@@ -1 +1,18 @@
+require 'fileutils'
+include FileUtils
 
+conflicts = `find ~/Dropbox -name "*conflicted*"`.split("\n")
+same, diff = conflicts.select { |conflict|
+  actual = conflict.sub(/ \(.*'s conflicted copy \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\)/, '')
+  diff = `diff "#{actual}" "#{conflict}"`
+  diff.empty?
+}
+
+same.each do |conflict|
+  rm conflict
+end
+
+puts diff.map { |conflict|
+  [conflict, diff].join("\n")
+}.join("\n")
+

+"""
+Hook wrapper "result" utilities.
+"""
+import sys
+import warnings
 
+_py3 = sys.version_info > (3, 0)
+
+
+if not _py3:
+    exec(
+        """
+def _reraise(cls, val, tb):
+    raise cls, val, tb
+"""
+    )
+
+
+def _raise_wrapfail(wrap_controller, msg):
+    co = wrap_controller.gi_code
+    raise RuntimeError(
+        "wrap_controller at %r %s:%d %s"
+        % (co.co_name, co.co_filename, co.co_firstlineno, msg)
+    )
+
+
+class HookCallError(Exception):
+    """ Hook was called wrongly. """
+
+
+class _Result(object):
+    def __init__(self, result, excinfo):
+        self._result = result
+        self._excinfo = excinfo
+
+    @property
+    def excinfo(self):
+        return self._excinfo
+
+    @property
+    def result(self):
+        """Get the result(s) for this hook call (DEPRECATED in favor of ``get_result()``)."""
+        msg = "Use get_result() which forces correct exception handling"
+        warnings.warn(DeprecationWarning(msg), stacklevel=2)
+        return self._result
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_call(cls, func):
+        __tracebackhide__ = True
+        result = excinfo = None
+        try:
+            result = func()
+        except BaseException:
+            excinfo = sys.exc_info()
+
+        return cls(result, excinfo)
+
+    def force_result(self, result):
+        """Force the result(s) to ``result``.
+
+        If the hook was marked as a ``firstresult`` a single value should
+        be set otherwise set a (modified) list of results. Any exceptions
+        found during invocation will be deleted.
+        """
+        self._result = result
+        self._excinfo = None
+
+    def get_result(self):
+        """Get the result(s) for this hook call.
+
+        If the hook was marked as a ``firstresult`` only a single value
+        will be returned otherwise a list of results.
+        """
+        __tracebackhide__ = True
+        if self._excinfo is None:
+            return self._result
+        else:
+            ex = self._excinfo
+            if _py3:
+                raise ex[1].with_traceback(ex[2])
+            _reraise(*ex)  # noqa
+

CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.

Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.

state:
CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.

controller.instructions: Who is the ultimate controller of Nimbus?
controller.label: c

interest.instructions: What is Topaz's economic interest in Nimbus? Round to two decimal places.
interest.label: a

state:
CORPORATE HOLDINGS REGISTER
Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.
Yarrow owns 65.00% of Nimbus.
Lagoon owns 35.00% of Nimbus.
Topaz owns 75.00% of Yarrow.
